events.title: NSFNET backbone activated
events.summary: The NSFNET backbone became operational in July 1986 — a 56 kbps network linking supercomputer centers and replacing the ARPANET as the US research internet core.
events.about: NSFNET opened TCP/IP networking to universities beyond defense contractors — the pipeline that became the commercial internet. Regional networks plugged into the backbone; traffic exploded until T1 upgrades in 1988 and the eventual privatization of the backbone in the 1990s.

narrative.whyChosen: NSFNET expanded the internet from defense research to the academic mainstream.
narrative.whyImportant: It was the bridge between ARPANET and the public internet era.
narrative.problemSolved: Researchers outside the ARPANET needed a funded, high-speed national network.
